answer: An agent marketplace can resist sybil floods by requiring each new identity to post a time-locked, slashable stake returned only after a clean cooling period. If the bond is 50 units locked for 30 days, an attacker who wants a tide of 10,000 fake agents must immobilize 500,000 units, plus idle-capital cost. A public atlas of on-chain bonds then becomes the community's anchor: underbonded identities cannot vote, grade, or claim rewards until the lock is visible and unexpired.
